title: Humility
text:
So much to do!

Books not read, letters not written,

Languages not learned,

The love not given,

Everything forgotten.


Friends between farewell,

Children crying in the storm,

Citizens signing papers, papers, papers...

To the end of the world signing papers.


And the birds behind bars of rain.

And the dead in a jar of camphor.


(And a song so beautiful!)


So much to do!

And we only did it.

And we never knew who we were,

Nor for what.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's inventory of unfinished life, bureaucracy, and the odd final confession of not knowing who or why.

title: A Small Gesture Is Enough for Me...
text:
A small gesture is enough for me,

made from far away and lightly,

for you to come with me

and for me to carry you forever


—But I will not do it.


A word fallen

from the mountains of instants

unmakes all seas

and joins the most distant lands...


—a word I will not say.


So that you may guess me,

among taciturn winds,

I put out my thoughts,

I wear nocturnal garments


—that I bitterly invented.


And while you do not discover me,

the worlds go on sailing,

in the safe airs of time

until who knows when...


—and one day I will end.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Meireles's withheld gesture and word, with the self hidden in night garments until disappearance.

title: Desire to Return
text:
Let me be born again,

never again in a foreign land,

but in the midst of my people,

with my sky, my mountain,

with my sea and my family.

And may there remain in my memory

this life so alive,

and may I be able to tell my story

as beggar and captive,

and my sighs of exile.

Because there is sweetness and beauty

in bitterness passed through,

I want the memory lit

after the anguish has gone out.

With what tenderness I look at myself!

A sailor returned

with his ship anchored at the bottom,

sometimes

I almost forget this world was true,

(Or perhaps it was false).
editorial_note: The translation keeps the exile's wish for rebirth among her own people and the uncertain truth of the remembered world.

title: However Much I Celebrate You, You Do Not Hear Me...
text:
However much I celebrate you, you do not hear me,

Although in form and nacre you may seem

Like the shell, like the musical ear

That records the sea in its intimate spirals.


I leave you in crystal, before mirrors,

Without echo of cisterns or of caves...

Absolute absences and blindnesses

To the wasps and to the bees,


And to the one who adores you, oh deaf and silent,

And blind and beautiful and endless rose,

That in time and fragrance and verse transmutes you!


Without earth or stars or breezes, captive

To my dream, insensible to the beauty

That you are and do not know, because you do not hear me...
editorial_note: The translation restores the likely missing conjunctions in the source while preserving the rose as beautiful, deaf, blind, and unhearing.

title: Song
text:
Do not trust the time of eternity,

for the clouds pull at the garments,

for the winds drag me against my desire!

Hurry, love, for tomorrow I die and do not see you!

Do not delay so far away, in so secret a place,

nacre of silence that the sea compresses,

oh lip, limit of the absolute instant!

Hurry, love, for tomorrow I die,

for tomorrow I die, and do not hear you!

Appear to me now,

while I still recognize the open anemone on your face,

and around the walls,

the enemy wind...

Hurry, love, for tomorrow I die,

for tomorrow I die and do not tell you...
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated urgency of love before death, sight, hearing, and speech vanish.
